text:
Ryan O'Reilly is 35, has more than 900 career points, and is quietly one of the league's most valuable forwards in close games. By our wins added measure, which credits each goal for how much it swung the win chance, he ranks 26th of 547 skaters. His two goals in Vegas on Nov. 13 helped Nashville to a seventh straight win, haunting the Knights "again," as Vegas Hockey Knight put it.

Nine goals and 20 points in 22 games, half on the power play, is right in line with his talent range. The finishing runs hot (22% shooting on 6.63 expected goals), but his on-ice luck is near zero, so the points are mostly honest.

The worry is five-on-five. Nashville gets only 45.9% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and that was before back-to-back losses to San Jose and Minnesota. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking still shows the playmaker who won the Conn Smythe in 2019: 9.9 primary shot assists per 60, 93rd percentile among forwards.
headline: O'Reilly is still Nashville's quiet difference maker
